learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge about the selection of industrial application materials, such as selection limits and indices.
Acquire knowledge about the selection of materials with industrial application, highlighting the characteristics of each group of materials: metallic, ceramic, polymeric and composite.
Acquire knowledge about computer-assisted material selection, focusing on database-type programs.

Through the preparation of a practical case of material selection or substitution, students will be able to select the most convenient and optimal materials, which meet a series of demands and characteristics, to develop an industrial product.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Knowledge and capacities for the application of materials engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to materials selection and utilization. Strategies and general processes in materials selection.
Failure analysis in service and substitution of damaged materials.
Selection and utilization of metallic materials. Metals: ferrous and non-ferrous. Properties of metals. Selection of metallic materials.
Selection and utilization of ceramic materials and glasses. Ceramics. Properties of structural ceramics. Glasses. Design and selection of ceramics and glasses.
Selection and utilization of polymeric materials. Structural characteristics and fundamental properties of polymers. Properties used in polymer design. Selection of polymeric materials.
Selection and utilization of composite materials. Properties of composite materials used in design. Selection of composite materials.
Introduction to computer-aided material selection. Types of programs used in computer-aided material selection.
Computerized databases for material selection: Introduction to Granta EduPack program.

Material selection using Granta EduPack program. Selection diagrams. Limit and tree diagrams. Creation and interpretation of Ashby diagrams. Material selection using complex graphical representations.

Handling material selection criteria using Granta EduPack program. Introduction of design requirements in Granta EduPack program. Limit stages. Selection indices. Use of more than one selection index.
Selection of production processes using Granta EduPack program. Cost estimation tool per part. Selection of production processes based on cost per part and cost of each process.
Selection of advanced materials with specific properties: sandwich panels, multi-layer structures, composite materials.
Selection of ecological materials using the Granta EduPack ecological audit. Product life cycle. Energy consumption and carbon footprint.
Strategies for minimizing environmental impact and material selection.
teaching_methods: Elaboration and presentation of a collective work on a practical case of material selection
Lectures for the exposition of course content
Computer practical sessions in an IT classroom in small groups
Resolution of practical cases of material selection in the classroom

assessment_methods.method: Written test 1 on Block I contents
Written test 2 on Block II contents
Submission and resolution of problems and practical cases

assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is the general model. A minimum grade of 5.0 is required in each written test to pass the course. Written tests not passed can be re-evaluated in the extraordinary call. The final grade is the weighted average of the assessment activities, provided all minimum grades are met and the average is at least 5.0. If minimum grades are not met, the final grade will be the average of the written tests, not exceeding 4.5. In the extraordinary call, students retake only the re-evaluable activities they did not pass.
